cases.name: Karin Schiffer Evans
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Karin had a passion for science and pursued a degree in microbiology graduating with her Masters from the University of Massachusetts Amherst. She began her career as a research immunologist at T Cell sciences in Cambridge MA. She eventually retired her microscope and decided to start a family, having her first daughter Joanne followed by twins, Carolyn and John.  

Throughout her entire life, Karin had a love for music, animals, the great outdoors, and cooking. Karin knew how to play three instruments, the piano, the flute and the guitar. At family Christmas celebrations you could find her sitting behind the piano playing music for the family to joyfully sing along to. She enjoyed riding and taking care of  horses, and shared that love with her daughter, Carolyn. She enjoyed preparing dinners and desserts; whether it be a grapenut pudding or Indian pudding, shortbread cookies, Boston cream pie, German potato salad or a weisswurst and sauerkraut. She was frugal and embodied the traits of a do-it-yourselfer. She could often be found tinkering on her own vehicles to repair them herself, or tending to flowers in her garden. She had a love for the mountains, camping, water skiing in Vermont, and down-hill skiing in the winter. In the summers, you could find her on a floatie in the ocean, swimming in the pool with her nieces and nephews, or eating a large plate of fried clam strips. Karin could talk for hours, and always ended phone calls with at least three goodbyes.  

Karin was benevolent and smart. She had a big heart. She is so loved and will be missed dearly."
